title: What is data?
text:
Data is recorded information. Good analysis starts by understanding what each value represents.
You are helping a fictional mobile-money service, NilePay, understand its payments. We start with six receipts, not a complicated AI model.
A missing value is unknown, not automatically zero. A count of receipts is not the same as their total value.
What is one row in a payments table?
Keep a data dictionary: column name, meaning, type, unit, allowed values, and source. This prevents incorrect business conclusions before coding begins.
Data means recorded observations. A receipt records who paid, how much, when, and whether it succeeded. A record is one receipt; a field is one property such as amo

title: Files, memory, and pressing Run
text:
A computer accepts input, follows instructions, stores state, and produces output.
Before writing code, know where the instructions and data live. You can complete this course in a browser without installing Python.
A .py extension alone does not make prose valid Python. A shell command such as python hello.py belongs in a terminal, not inside a Python script.
What does a Python interpreter do?
For later desktop practice: install Python 3 from its official site, save hello.py, and run python hello.py in a terminal in the same folder. The in-course labs are browser simulations; the code panels are Python examples to copy into a real interpreter.
A computer stores files persistently on storage

title: Numbers, units, and notation
text:
An integer is a whole number, such as 6.
Percentages, arrays, and learning algorithms all reuse ordinary arithmetic. We build this bridge before using mathematical symbols.
Percent and percentage points differ: moving from 40% to 50% is +10 percentage points, but a 25% relative increase.
How do you convert 0.25 into a percentage?
Always check units before combining columns. Divide total successful value by successful receipt count for average successful payment value; do not divide by all receipts.
An integer is a whole number, such as 6. A decimal such as 3.14 is represented in Python by float. Negative values represent amounts below zero, such as a reversal adjustment.; Multiplication uses

title: Names, values, and types
text:
A variable is a name bound to a value so a program can reuse and change state.
A receipt processor needs to remember an amount and a status. Variables give these values useful names.
Do not use a Python keyword such as for as a name. Avoid overwriting built-ins such as list or print.
What is the type of "120"?
Python variables refer to objects; they are not fixed typed boxes. Later, two names can refer to one mutable list. Learn this distinction before reasoning about copies.
amount = 120 associates the name amount with the integer 120. The = sign assigns a value; it does not ask whether two values are equal. You can reassign the name later.; Python names may contain letters, digits, and und

title: Arithmetic and comparisons in Python
text:
Operators combine values into expressions: arithmetic, comparison, and boolean logic.
Compute fees correctly and distinguish a calculation from a decision.
Integer // is not ordinary decimal division, and it does not always round toward zero. Binary floating-point cannot represent every decimal exactly; use integer minor units or Decimal for exact money.
Which expression asks whether x equals 5?
When reporting money, decide a rounding policy. Rounding every row before aggregation can differ from rounding the final sum. Write a test that fixes the business rule.
+ adds numbers, - subtracts, * multiplies, / divides, and ** raises to a power. For x=5 and y=2, x+y is 7 and x/y is 2.5.; // perfor

title: Text, input, and conversion
text:
A str is a sequence of characters.
People type text, even when the text looks like a number. A payment form must convert and validate it.
Converting a customer identifier to an integer can lose leading zeros. Identifiers are labels; keep them as strings.
What does input() return?
Validate ranges as well as types. Successfully converting "-100" does not mean a new payment should accept it. Errors and validation will be taught with file handling.
A str is a sequence of characters. "Hello" and 'Hello' are equivalent ways to write text. Indexes start at zero: "Nile"[0] is "N".; input("Amount: ") prompts a person and returns a string. int(...) converts whole-number text and float(...) converts de

title: Decisions and indentation
text:
Conditionals choose which block of code runs based on a boolean expression.
NilePay should accept a positive amount and reject zero or negative amounts. That requires branching.
Missing line breaks or unexpected indentation can make an assessment snippet invalid. Interpret code as displayed, and distinguish a formatting repair from actual Python behavior.
What marks the body of an if statement in Python?
Keep business rules readable. Nested conditions can hide edge cases; test the boundary amount=0 explicitly.
if tests a condition. If it is True, Python executes the indented block beneath it. A colon starts the block, and consistent indentation shows which statements belong to it.; else hand

title: Lists, indexing, and list arithmetic
text:
Square brackets create a list: [10, 20, 30].
A variable holds one amount; a list holds an ordered collection of amounts.
The original list MCQ has no valid choice. Curly braces create a set, parentheses create a tuple, and adding an integer to a list is invalid. Do not learn the forced-choice guess as Python.
Which expression creates [1, 2, 3]?
A shallow copy makes a new outer list but shares nested objects. Use a deep copy only when you actually need independent nested structures.
Square brackets create a list: [10, 20, 30]. Its length is 3. Index 0 means the first item; index -1 means the last. items[1:3] selects indexes 1 and 2, excluding stop index 3.; Lists are mutable: append(40) adds

title: Tuples, sets, dictionaries, and identity
text:
Python collections store multiple values with different ordering, mutability, and lookup behavior.
Choose a container based on the question: preserve an order, remove duplicates, or look up a value by a key.
Use == for ordinary value comparisons. Use is None for checking None, the singleton representing absence. A dictionary is not created by {1,2,3}; that is a set.
What does b = a do when a is a list?
Lists support positional access; dictionaries and sets usually provide fast membership lookup. The algorithm lesson will explain why choosing the right container changes runtime.
A tuple is an ordered collection whose slots cannot be reassigned. Write (1, 2, 3); a one-item tuple needs a comma:

title: Loops and accumulators
text:
Loops repeat a block over a sequence or while a condition remains true.
Calculate a total from many receipts without writing the same operation over and over.
print inside the loop prints intermediate values; print after the loop prints the final result. Their indentation changes behavior.
Which values does range(3) produce?
A list comprehension is a concise transformation: [a*2 for a in amounts]. Learn the equivalent loop first so you can debug filters and nested comprehensions.
for visits each item in a sequence. In for amount in amounts, amount is assigned a new item on each iteration. The indented body runs once for that item.; range(3) produces 0, 1, 2. The stop value is excluded. range

title: Functions, arguments, and return
text:
Functions package reusable behavior behind a name, inputs, and an optional return value.
A fee calculation should be defined once and reused consistently for every payment.
Writing fee without parentheses refers to the function; it does not call it. Returning a value is different from printing it.
Which keyword defines a function?
A pure function depends only on its inputs and avoids changing outside state. Pure transformations make data pipelines easier to test and rerun.
def introduces a function. Its name describes the action; parameters are names for the inputs. The indented body is saved for later, not executed when the definition is encountered.; Calling fee(100) runs the body with amo

title: Local, global, and nonlocal scope
text:
Scope controls where a name can be read or changed and prevents unrelated code from colliding.
The same name can exist in different places. Trace which variable an assignment changes before predicting output.
Using a local name before its assignment can raise UnboundLocalError. A global declaration is not itself an error, but unnecessary shared state complicates testing.
Which keyword rebinds a variable in an enclosing function?
Nested example: outer sets x="outer x"; inner declares nonlocal x and sets it to "inner x". Printing inside inner and then inside outer prints "inner x" twice.
A function normally creates local names. Reading a name searches local, enclosing function, global module,

title: The mutable default argument trap
text:
Default arguments are evaluated once, when def runs.
A helper that collects receipts can accidentally remember previous calls. This bug appears in the AI assessment.
Do not confuse this with list concatenation. The shared object persists because it is the same default, not because all lists are global.
What is the usual safe default for an optional new list?
Safe version: def add(x, items=None): create items=[] if items is None, then append and return. If a caller deliberately passes a list, document whether your function mutates it.
Default arguments are evaluated once, when def runs. A default [] is one list reused by calls that omit that argument.; If the function appends 1 on its first c

title: Files, exceptions, and safe cleanup
text:
Context managers close files reliably, even when an error occurs.
Read receipts from a saved file, and ensure resources are closed even when an error occurs.
The reading-mode question has two valid answers: explicit "r" and omitted mode. w can destroy existing content. file.close is a reference; file.close() actually calls the method.
Which statement is true?
CSV contains rows and columns with quoting rules; use the csv module or pandas rather than splitting every line on a comma. Specify encoding, preserve identifiers as strings, and validate headers.

title: Modules, environments, and reproducibility
text:
Modules organize code; packages distribute it; environments isolate dependencies.
NumPy and pandas are reusable libraries. Keeping their versions recorded makes an example reproducible.
This HTML does not install or run these Python packages. Its local labs compute the taught mechanisms in JavaScript, with explicit controls and formulas.
Why record dependency versions?
Use a requirements or lock file and a clean-environment installation test for a real project. Installation needs internet initially unless you already have the packages locally.
A module is reusable Python code. import math loads a module; math.sqrt(9) calls its square-root function. A package groups related modules.; import n

title: Objects and small, testable programs
text:
An object combines state and operations.
A payment has related properties and behavior. A class can keep them together without duplicating rules.
A class definition is not the same as an instance. Avoid putting a mutable per-instance list at class scope, where instances may share it.
What does self refer to?
Dependency injection means supplying a dependency, such as a database connection, from outside. It allows a test to provide a fake connection without contacting a real server.
An object combines state and operations. A class is a definition for creating objects. __init__ initializes a new object, and self refers to the current instance.; A method is a function attached to a class. Differ

title: Data structures and algorithm cost
text:
An algorithm is a sequence of steps that transforms input into output.
Your six receipts will eventually become six million. An algorithm that repeatedly scans everything may stop being practical.
Fast code that deletes legitimate repeated payments is wrong. Define a unique transaction key before deduplicating.
Which structure naturally supports unique membership?
Advanced practice: compare sliding windows for rolling totals, recursion for tree traversal, dynamic programming for repeated subproblems, and greedy choices only when they can be justified. Measure runtime and memory rather than guessing.

title: Testing, debugging, and Git
text:
A unit test checks one small behavior.
A passing quiz is useful; a repeatable test against your code is stronger evidence.
A green test only proves what it checks. Do not commit secrets, real customer records, or generated virtual environments to a repository.
What is a useful boundary test for positive payment amounts?
For real projects add type hints, linting, test automation in CI, meaningful README instructions, and a rollback commit/tag. Test contracts and invariants; do not merely duplicate the implementation in a test.
A unit test checks one small behavior. Arrange input, call the function, then assert the expected result. An integration test checks components working together.; Test

title: NumPy: arrays, axes, and shape
text:
A NumPy array stores same-typed values in an efficient n-dimensional structure.
Lists hold collections; NumPy arrays organize numerical values for efficient calculations. Think of receipts arranged on a numbered grid.
Shape is not the total element count. A shape of (6,) is neither (1,6) nor (6,1).
What does arr.shape return?
Array storage is usually homogeneous. Choose integer or floating-point precision deliberately; unsigned integers cannot represent negative values.
An array has a shape, a tuple containing the length of each axis. [1,2,3] has shape (3,), one axis of length three. The comma makes it a one-item tuple.; A 2-by-3 table has shape (2,3): axis 0 selects rows and axis 1 selects

title: Dtypes, precision, and memory
text:
The dtype controls representation, memory use, precision, and valid operations.
A million receipt amounts take space. Choosing their representation affects memory, precision, and which values you can store.
nbytes is the array element buffer, not the total memory used by your whole process.
What can change when you change dtype?
Estimate the element buffer for one million float32 values and float64 values. Then measure a real array and distinguish buffer memory from process memory. Explain how your payment representation handles negative refunds.
A bit holds one binary digit, 0 or 1. Eight bits make a byte. A fixed-width dtype specifies how an array element is represented: int32 uses 32 bits

title: Index, slice, reshape, and reduce
text:
Indexing selects elements; slicing selects ranges without writing manual loops.
Select one receipt, rearrange a grid without changing its values, or total each day.
Axis specifies what is reduced, not the shape you want to keep. Reshaping does not sort values.
Can six values be reshaped into (4,2)?
Advanced: strides describe how moving along an axis moves through memory. A view can be cheap but shares changes; a copy takes extra memory.

title: Adding dimensions: newaxis, expand_dims, ndmin
text:
np.newaxis and expand_dims insert a size-1 axis so shapes can align.
Sometimes the values are right but their orientation is wrong. Adding a length-one axis makes the intended calculation explicit.
ndmin does not normalize data, force integer type, or specify a minimum value. It specifies a minimum number of axes.
Which function inserts an axis at a chosen position?
Use explicit row/column shapes before broadcasting. squeeze removes length-one axes, but removing a batch axis accidentally can break a model.

title: Broadcasting, from the last axis backward
text:
Broadcasting performs element-wise operations on different but compatible shapes.
Apply a separate adjustment to each of three payment columns across every row without a Python loop.
Do not compare from the first axis. Broadcasting is conceptual reuse, not a promise that the entire result uses no memory.
When are aligned axis lengths compatible?
Accidental (n,1)+(n,) creates n-by-n values. Check shapes before running a large job; a silent valid broadcast can still implement the wrong mathematics.
Broadcasting combines compatible shapes for element-wise arithmetic. Compare their axes from the rightmost end, padding the shorter shape on the left with conceptual ones.; At each aligned axis, len

title: Sorting values versus sorting indexes
text:
Sorting returns ordered values; argsort returns the indices that would produce that order.
Rank payment amounts while keeping the original receipt IDs attached.
Tied values can have different relative orders depending on the sorting method. Request a stable method when retaining tie order matters.
Which function returns indexes that would sort an array?
Document ascending/descending and tie rules in reports. Sorting one column alone in a separate object can detach it from other fields.
np.sort(a) returns sorted values. np.argsort(a) returns the original indexes in the order that would sort the values.; For [30,10,20], the smallest value lives at index 1, followed by index 2, then index 0. ar

title: pandas Series and custom labels
text:
A Series is a one-dimensional labeled array whose index participates in alignment.
A numeric vector becomes easier to interpret when every value has a meaningful label.
A Series can contain strings and have non-unique labels. This course uses unique labels for alignment examples so the behavior is clear.
A Series is best described as what?
Index labels are part of computation, not merely decoration. The next lesson shows why reordering labels changes a position-based calculation but not a label-aligned one.
A pandas Series is a one-dimensional labeled array. It combines values with an index of labels. Labels can be strings, dates, or other supported hashable values.; pd.Series([100,200],inde

title: Series arithmetic aligns labels
text:
pandas aligns values by labels, which is powerful but can introduce missing values if labels differ.
Costs and receipt counts may arrive in a different order. pandas matches the labels before multiplying.
Shared labels do not mean multiplication ignores indexes. Duplicated indexes introduce additional alignment cases beyond this unique-label example.
What determines which values multiply?
Use alignment as a data quality check: inspect missing and duplicate keys before merging measures from different reports.
Let S1 have A=10 and B=20. Let S2 arrive as B=3 and A=2. Matching rows by position would pair A with B incorrectly.; S1*S2 matches A to A and B to B. The results are A=20 and B=60, regar

title: DataFrames: a spreadsheet with an API
text:
A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled table, similar to a spreadsheet or SQL result.
Organize all receipt fields together so filtering an amount also keeps its correct ID and status.
Both Series and DataFrame support labels and are used in analysis. Neither automatically saves your results to a file.
Which structure most resembles a spreadsheet or SQL table?
Use explicit dtypes when importing large files and identifiers. For large CSVs use chunksize, but global deduplication and aggregates need state across chunks.
A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled data structure with rows and columns. Different columns can have different types.; Construct a DataFrame from a dictionary of same-leng

title: Filter, clean, and validate data
text:
Cleaning makes types, missing values, duplicates, and invalid records explicit before analysis.
An attractive chart cannot repair duplicate receipts or missing amounts. Validate before analysis.
Filling a missing transaction amount with zero can hide a reporting failure. Use .loc for assignment instead of chained indexing.
What should determine a missing-value policy?
For model preprocessing, learn filling values on training data only. Using all rows before splitting leaks information from future evaluation data.
Filtering keeps rows that satisfy a condition: df.loc[df["status"]=="OK"]. loc selects labels or Boolean masks; iloc selects positions.; Check missingness with isna(), not equality

title: Group, aggregate, and sort
text:
GroupBy follows split → apply → combine to summarize rows by category.
Turn individual receipts into an operator report: total successful value per operator.
count counts non-missing values, while size counts rows. Avoid blindly summing identifier or text columns; select the numeric measure explicitly.
What can the by argument in sort_values accept?
An average of group averages can be wrong when group sizes differ. Recompute from total value divided by total valid count, or use appropriate weights.
groupby separates records by matching key values. An aggregation such as sum, count, or mean computes one result for each group.; df.groupby("operator")["amount"].sum() produces a Series of totals

title: Matplotlib: make a chart understandable
text:
A useful plot encodes a question clearly, labels axes, and gives legends only when needed.
A plot should answer a question without making the reader guess what its lines and units mean.
Calling legend() without meaningful labels may produce no useful entries. A truncated y-axis can exaggerate changes; state the scale clearly.
Which functions label axes?
Explore distributions and outliers before modeling. Separate measures by relevant groups; a combined trend can hide opposite group-level patterns.
Choose a chart for the question: a line shows a time trend, bars compare categories, a histogram shows a distribution, and a scatter plot compares two numeric variables.; plt.plot(x,y,label="...")

title: Exploration before explanation
text:
EDA checks shape, distributions, missingness, relationships, and suspicious values before conclusions.
A report can look polished while hiding missing receipts or one giant outlier. Exploration checks whether the data can support your question.
Finding a relationship does not prove that changing one variable will cause the other to change.
What should happen before interpreting a surprising average?
Write a one-page exploration memo: question, data dictionary, quality findings, two charts with units, three observations, and two unanswered questions. Trace every claim back to rows.
Start with provenance, time coverage, row count, column meanings, and the unit of observation. EDA means explora

title: SQL: ask a table a question
text:
SQL declaratively asks a relational database to filter, project, group, and combine rows.
The same operations used in pandas appear in databases. SQL asks for a result without spelling out each row iteration.
WHERE amount = NULL does not test missingness. Rows have no guaranteed order without ORDER BY.
Which expression tests a missing amount?
The browser lab implements the shown filter and aggregate operations; it is not a complete SQL server. For independent work run the supplied query in SQLite or PostgreSQL with the course CSV imported.
A relational database stores tables with schemas. A primary key uniquely identifies a row; a foreign key refers to a key in another table.; SELECT chooses

title: Joins, keys, and double-counting
text:
A join combines rows from tables using a relationship key; join type determines unmatched-row behavior.
Attach operator names to payment receipts while proving that no money was multiplied by duplicate keys.
Adding DISTINCT after a bad join can hide the cause. Fix the relationship and grain—the meaning of one row.
What does a left join preserve?
Compare row count, distinct receipt count, and total amount before and after a join. All three checks reveal different classes of mistakes.
An INNER JOIN retains matching pairs. A LEFT JOIN retains every left row and fills missing right-side fields with NULL. RIGHT and FULL joins preserve the corresponding other sides.; The ON condition defines the m

title: Relational modeling and update anomalies
text:
Keys, constraints, and normalized relationships protect meaning and reduce update anomalies.
If an operator changes its display name, you should not have to repair thousands of historical receipt rows by hand.
A negative amount may represent a legitimate refund. A database check must reflect the actual business policy.
Why keep operator details in a separate table?
Draw receipt, operator, and receipt-item tables. Mark their keys and relationship cardinalities. Explain why summing receipt totals after an item join can duplicate money.
Choose the grain: what exactly does one row represent? A receipt table has one row per receipt, while a receipt-item table has one row per item. Mixing grains c

title: CTEs, windows, and latest records
text:
Window functions calculate across related rows without collapsing them into one row per group.
Find the latest login per operator or the highest payment per group without collapsing all row details.
A window ORDER BY does not guarantee final display order. A fallback value may be stale; expose its date rather than hiding that fact.
How do window functions differ from GROUP BY?
Extend to cumulative totals, LAG for period changes, and gaps-and-islands grouping. Verify window frames explicitly, especially with tied timestamps.
A CTE, introduced by WITH, gives a subquery a readable name. It helps separate stages; it is not automatically a performance optimization.; A window function computes ove

title: Indexes and reading execution plans
text:
Indexes trade write/storage cost for faster selective reads; query plans show how the database executes a query.
An index is like a book index: it helps locate matching rows without reading every page, at an additional maintenance cost.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually executes a statement in systems such as PostgreSQL. Use care with modifying statements and production workloads.
Why not index every column?
Benchmark row-oriented versus columnar analytical storage, partition pruning, and predicate pushdown. Do not promise fixed speedups without measuring the workload.
A B-tree index keeps ordered keys and references to data. It often supports equality, ranges, and ordering. Other index types have di

title: Transactions and parameterized CRUD
text:
Transactions provide atomicity and isolation so multi-step changes remain consistent under failure and concurrency.
A transfer should debit one account and credit another as one reliable unit of work.
Do not paste user values into SQL with f-strings. A rollback cannot undo an email or other external effect already sent.
What does atomicity mean?
For independent work implement transfer(amount) with insufficient-funds checks, concurrent tests, idempotency, and reconciliation of before/after balances.
CRUD means create, read, update, delete. Database applications should validate inputs and use parameterized queries instead of constructing SQL from user text.; A transaction groups changes. Atomi

title: Networks, HTTP, and APIs
text:
An API exposes controlled operations over HTTP; JSON commonly carries structured request and response data.
A reporting script may need to ask a service for data. Understand the request before building an AI agent that calls tools.
A successful HTTP status does not prove the data is complete. Retrying a non-idempotent write can create duplicates.
What does authorization decide?
TCP delivers ordered reliable byte streams; UDP trades that machinery for a simpler datagram service. Production clients need timeout budgets, bounded retries with backoff, and a clear error contract.
A client sends a request; a server handles it. An IP address identifies a network destination, a port identifies a ser

title: Powers, roots, exponentials, and logarithms
text:
Powers model repeated multiplication; logarithms invert exponentials and appear throughout loss functions and numerical computing.
The symbols used in scaling, sigmoid, and cross-entropy are ordinary numerical functions. Learn what they do before meeting them inside a model.
In Python ** is exponentiation. The ^ operator is not the ordinary exponentiation operator. log(0) is not a finite real value.
What is the square root of 9?
When exponentiating large scores, subtract their maximum before computing softmax probabilities. This leaves normalized probabilities unchanged and reduces overflow risk.
A power repeats multiplication: 3 squared is 3*3=9. A square root reverses squaring for nonnegat

title: Mean, median, spread, and outliers
text:
Mean, median, spread, and quantiles summarize data but never replace examining the distribution.
Before predicting payments, describe what an ordinary day looks like and how much it varies.
Standard deviation is not the average amount. A large outlier may be valid; investigate rather than automatically deleting it.
Which summary resists a single extreme outlier more?
NumPy std uses ddof=0 by default; pandas Series.std uses ddof=1 by default. State which definition you used when reconciling reports.
The mean is the sum divided by the count. For [10,20,30], the mean is 20. The median is the middle value after sorting; for an even count average the two middle values.; An outlier is unusually fa

title: Probability and conditional reasoning
text:
Probability represents uncertainty; conditional probability updates belief when information changes.
A fraud model predicts uncertainty, not certainty. Learn the denominator before reading a probability.
High overall accuracy can hide failure on the rare class. Correlation does not establish a causal effect.
What does P(fraud | alert) condition on?
Bayes rule combines prior probability and evidence: P(A|B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B). Start with a frequency table rather than memorizing symbols without denominators.
Probability is a number from 0 to 1 describing likelihood under a model. 0 means impossible under that model and 1 means certain. Observed frequency estimates it from data.; P(A|B) means prob

title: Distributions, expectation, and normal noise
text:
A distribution describes possible random outcomes and their probabilities; expectation summarizes long-run average behavior.
A single average cannot describe uncertainty. A probability distribution describes which values can occur and how likely they are.
A normal distribution is not a synonym for any ordinary dataset. Real payment amounts are often skewed and may not follow a bell curve.
What characterizes standard-normal noise?
For independent work generate repeated samples, plot a histogram, compare empirical and expected means, and quantify the variability of the sample average. Larger samples reduce sampling uncertainty under appropriate assumptions.

title: Vectors, matrices, and weighted sums
text:
Vectors hold features; matrices transform them; dot products measure weighted alignment.
A model turns several measurements into one prediction. Vectors organize measurements; dot products combine them.

title: Derivatives and gradient descent
text:
A derivative measures how an output changes when an input changes by a tiny amount.
A model needs to know which way to adjust a weight to reduce its error. The derivative supplies a local direction.
A huge learning rate can overshoot or diverge. A tiny rate may converge slowly. Moving against the gradient is local improvement, not proof of a global optimum.
Which direction does gradient descent move?
Partial derivatives hold other variables fixed. Real neural losses are non-convex; monitor validation performance and numerical stability rather than assuming a unique best solution.

title: Machine learning, labels, and honest splits
text:
Define the target and metric, split data, establish a baseline, train, evaluate, and inspect errors.
Use rules when you know the rule; learn from examples when a useful pattern is difficult to write explicitly.
A feature recorded after an outcome can leak the answer. Excellent test accuracy from leakage does not represent deployable performance.
Which dataset should remain untouched until final evaluation?

title: StandardScaler and training-only fitting
text:
Scaling places numeric features on comparable ranges for algorithms sensitive to distance or gradient size.
A model based on distances can let large-valued features dominate. Standardization puts feature scales into comparable units.
Fitting the scaler on test data leaks evaluation information. A constant training feature has zero variance; StandardScaler handles its scaling without dividing by zero.
What does StandardScaler usually aim for on nonconstant training features?
Trees usually need less feature scaling than distance or gradient-based models. Outliers affect mean and variance; compare robust scaling when appropriate.
StandardScaler learns a mean and standard deviation for each feat

text:

text:
PCA projects data onto orthogonal directions that explain the most variance.
Many correlated measurements can repeat the same information. PCA builds fewer new features capturing large variation.
PCA is not a normalization method that guarantees values in [0,1]. Component values and signs should not be inferred solely from shape.

text:
Choose metrics that match the business error: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, MAE, MSE, and more.
A fraud-alert system needs to balance missed fraud with unnecessary investigations.
Accuracy alone can be misleading with imbalanced data. Handle undefined metrics explicitly when a denominator is zero.

text:
Pipelines fit preprocessing inside each training fold, reducing leakage and making evaluation reproducible.

Pipelines are not solely missing-value handlers or hyperparameter search tools. Ordinary random folds may be inappropriate for time series or repeated customers.

title: Decision trees and pruning
text:
Trees split feature space into rules; ensembles combine many trees to improve generalization.
A tree asks a sequence of questions, such as whether an amount exceeds a threshold, to arrive at a prediction.
Increasing depth usually increases capacity; it is not a standard way to prevent overfitting.

Inspect feature leakage and stability. An interpretable split can still encode a biased or unstable relationship.

text:
An ensemble combines multiple models.
Several imperfect models can make a more stable prediction when their errors differ.
Averaging models does not guarantee elimination of overfitting. Highly correlated errors limit ensemble benefits.

Boosting fits models sequentially to improve prior errors rather than independently averaging them. Compare forests and gradient boosting with the same validation policy.

text:

Group customers by behavior when no labeled category is available.

Evaluate stability, silhouette scores, and business usefulness. K-means prefers compact Euclidean clusters and can struggle with irregular shapes or outliers.

title: Neurons, layers, and nonlinearity
text:
A neuron computes a weighted sum plus bias and usually applies a nonlinear activation.
A neural network reuses the weighted sums you already learned, arranging them into trainable layers.
Deep learning can be supervised, self-supervised, or unsupervised. “Deep learning never needs labels” and “always needs more new data” are both too absolute.
What does a nonlinear activation add?
Choose output activation and loss together: raw logits for losses designed to accept logits, sigmoid for binary probability presentation, and softmax for mutually exclusive class probabilities.

title: Activation functions you can see
text:
Nonlinear activations let stacked layers represent relationships a purely linear network cannot.
A neuron needs more than a weighted sum to learn curved decision boundaries. An activation changes how its score becomes a signal.
Do not apply sigmoid or softmax twice when your loss already combines the transformation with the log-loss calculation.
What does nonlinearity allow a stacked network to represent?

text:
A loss turns prediction error into a scalar objective the optimizer can minimize.
A model needs a numerical definition of “wrong” before it can improve.
Applying sigmoid or softmax twice can create incorrect training behavior. Check what the loss function expects.
What does a loss quantify?
For an imbalanced task consider class weighting or sampling, then evaluate probability calibration and subgroup behavior. State which trade-off the loss encourages.

title: Autograd and the disconnected-loss trap
text:
Autograd records differentiable operations so gradients can be propagated backward through the computation graph.
Backpropagation can update a model only when its loss depends on that model through a differentiable computation.
Calling backward is not proof the desired model learned. Inspect parameter.grad and compare parameter values before and after optimizer.step().

Autograd accumulates gradients by default. Detaching a tensor or converting through a non-differentiable operation can break the graph. Some intentionally detached values are correct; document the purpose.

text:
Optimizers use gradients to update parameters; learning rate controls the update scale.
Follow one update in the correct order instead of treating “train” as a magical command.

text:
If identical neurons start with identical weights, they can learn the same features.
Weights must start somewhere. Poor initial scales can make signals vanish or explode before learning has a chance.

text:
Dropout randomly removes activations during training and rescales survivors to regularize a network.
Regularize a network so it cannot rely too strongly on a particular combination of features.
Dropout does not multiply every value by 0.5 and does not guarantee that exactly 50% of neurons are active.

Validate the rate for the architecture and data. Excessive dropout can underfit; stochastic regularization complicates reproducibility unless seeds and modes are controlled.

text:
Batch normalization normalizes intermediate activations and learns scale/shift parameters.
Keep intermediate activation scales manageable while the rest of the network changes during training.

text:
Generalization means performing well on unseen data; regularization and validation help detect overfitting.
A model should work on new payments, not merely remember historical ones.
Overfitting is not just “too many epochs.” Leakage, distribution shifts, and evaluation mistakes can also create confusing curves.
What is early stopping based on?
For advanced practice plot confidence intervals over repeated runs and evaluate drift, subgroup errors, calibration, and inference cost before selecting a model.

text:

What is the main reason to use a GPU for suitable ML workloads?
Profile compute and data-loading time separately. Mixed precision can improve speed and memory, but requires numerical checks and suitable hardware.

text:

text:

After detecting patterns, reduce spatial size so later layers can work with a more compact representation.

text:
RNNs carry hidden state through sequence positions, sharing parameters across time.
Payment history and text have order. A recurrent network carries a hidden state from one step to the next.

Backpropagation through time repeatedly multiplies derivatives. This can shrink or grow gradients strongly, motivating gated units and clipping.

text:
LSTMs use gates and a cell state to help preserve information across longer dependencies.
Long sequences can overwhelm a simple RNN. Gates regulate what is stored, forgotten, and exposed.

text:
Gradient clipping limits exploding gradients; attention provides a more direct way to focus on relevant positions.

Clipping does not directly solve vanishing gradients, and attention does not automatically prevent overfitting.

text:

text:

Create synthetic examples through a learning game between a producer and a critic.

title: Security and data governance

title: What a computer does
text:
A computer accepts input, follows instructions, stores state, and produces output.
Every later topic assumes you can reason about input, instructions, memory/state, and output. This gives you the mental model underneath code, data pipelines, and models.
Trace a receipt from keyboard/file input → memory → instructions → displayed result.
Confusing storage with memory, or assuming the computer “understands” intent instead of executing instructions.
